text: Merge and Append live in the same Combine group and both produce one result from two tables — which is exactly why analysts mix them up. They combine data in opposite directions.
Merge reaches sideways — it needs a shared key column, and adds new columns from another table. Append reaches downward — it needs the same columns in both tables, and adds more rows.

If you've used VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP, Merge is the same idea at table scale. Pick a matching column in each table — ProductID here, in both — and Power Query confirms how many rows matched before you even click OK.

Append assumes your tables already have the same shape — a January file and a February file, say — and just stacks one under the other. Two tables appends directly; three or more lets you build an ordered list, useful for a whole folder of monthly files.

Before reaching for either one, ask: do these tables share a key column I want to match on, or do they share the same columns and I just want more rows? Shared key — Merge. Same columns — Append. Getting this backward is the single most common Power Query mistake.
